thread.title: Apple: A Look at Its Moves in Digital Television

title: Apple: A Look at Its Moves in Digital Television
text:
Large Photo: Getty Images 
Apple, which has big aims of building a television business—part of a strategy to bolster growth with service revenue —is moving fast and spending money. 
That’s one way to read this Sunday New York Times feature examining those efforts, saying that the Barron’s Next 50 company’s plans “plans to make itself into a big player in the entertainment industry are now coming into focus” as it has begun to challenge traditional studios as well as digital players including Netflix (NFLX) and Facebook (FB). 
A few observations from the story: 
• The company is making itself attractive to creative talent. “Since October, Apple (AAPL) has made deals for 12 projects, nine of them “straight-to-series” orders—an aggressive method of creating new programming that skips the pilot-episode stage,” the Times wrote. “Apple’s strong brand name and its willingness to write big checks have quickly made it a top draw for show creators and stars.” 
• The programs may take a generally bright, upbeat tone. “It seems possible that Apple will shy away from projects that are gratuitously dark or heavy on social issues,” the Times reported. 
• Some pretty key details remain unclear. “Apple has not shared specifics with its new business partners on how it will distribute the shows, but they may be housed in its TV app, which allows access to video services like HBO Now and Hulu,” wrote the Times. “Nor has the company announced whether its projects will be behind a paywall, but the company will most likely require viewers to have subscriptions to access its shows at some point. 
The new programs could start rolling out in March 2019, the Times reported.
